title: Ephemeral turn-gating and memory-sculptor for streaming completions
creator: Aisha Desai
description:
Background: Streaming chat workloads produce many short, interleaved turns and frequent token-level responses. Our current continuous batching strategy sometimes creates microbatches that either (a) keep KV cache slots pinned longer than necessary for short ephemeral turns, or (b) expand GPU slab allocations for sessions that only need a brief response. This increases p95 latency under load and raises average GPU memory pressure.

Goal: Implement a set of heuristics ("turn-gating" + "memory-sculptor") that 1) gate microbatch formation for ephemeral turns to avoid inflating batch size or KV retention, and 2) proactively sculpt per-session GPU headroom and KV reservation to reduce fragmentation and evictions while preserving latency SLOs for streaming completions.

High-level approach:
- Turn-gating: classify a turn as ephemeral if predicted generated-token count <= N (configurable, default 12) using a lightweight stimulus estimator (user prompt length + recent session rate features). If ephemeral, prefer to route to a low-latency fast-path microbatcher with strict timeouts and limited queued depth.
- Memory-sculptor: maintain a per-session soft-headroom budget (tokens + kv-slot bytes). When multiple ephemeral turns compete, allow aggressive slot-sharing with TTL < T (configurable, default 2s) and a prioritized eviction order (background sessions -> low-priority sessions -> ephemeral short turns). Implement a compact-on-release hook that consolidates freed KV fragments immediately into GPU slab free-lists.
- Soft-deadlines & deadlines-aware packing: microbatcher observes per-request soft-deadline and forms bundles only if expected queuing + GPU slice time <= deadline; otherwise flows to an immediate single-request GPU slot.
- Prefetch trimming: when a session is flagged ephemeral, trim KV prefetching to only top-K recent tokens to reduce cache footprint.

Deliverables:
- Heuristic design document and config knobs (N, T, soft-headroom thresholds).
- Prototype implementation in continuous-batcher with feature flag runtime.ephemeral_gating.
- Integration with KV manager to support TTL and compact-on-release operations.
- Load test results showing quantifiable improvements (p95 latency, GPU mem utilization).

Why this is different from existing work: instead of only changing batch sizes or slab allocation, we combine request-level classification + per-session headroom shaping + immediate post-eviction consolidation to reduce both KV lifetime and slab fragmentation for streaming chat patterns.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Feature flag runtime.ephemeral_gating toggles the behavior and can be disabled without behavioral regressions; 2) On internal streaming chat benchmark (mix: 60% ephemeral turns <12 tokens, 40% longer turns), p95 latency for streaming completions improves by >=10% relative to baseline; 3) Average GPU memory fragmentation score reduces by >=8% and mean KV-resident bytes per-session drops by >=12%; 4) No increase in token-generation errors or returned partial completions in canary; 5) Unit and integration tests for gating logic, TTL eviction, and compact-on-release added

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Misclassification of ephemeral turns could starve longer-turn throughput. Mitigation: Conservative defaults (N=12), fallback path that permits immediate single-request GPU path when deadlines are tight.
Risk: Aggressive TTLs could thrash KV manager and increase RPCs to model host. Mitigation: rate-limit compact-on-release to X ops/s per-GPU; use adaptive backoff if eviction-induced misses spike.
Risk: Compact-on-release adds CPU overhead. Mitigation: offload consolidation to background worker with bounded CPU budget and use slab-free-list batch ops.
Risk: Interaction with autoscaler (Dedicated) causing oscillations when many ephemeral sessions free memory rapidly. Mitigation: add hysteresis window before signaling scale-down; prefer local headroom reuse.
test_plan: Unit tests: gating classifier, TTL eviction, compact-on-release hook, prefetch trimming. Integration tests: simulate mixed workload harness with representative short and long turns, validate lane selection and deadlines. Load testing: run A/B against production-like dataset on staging dedicated pool (48 A100s) measuring latency and GPU mem fragmentation. Canary rollout plan: enable flag for 5% of hosted traffic focusing on low-priority tenants, monitor key metrics for 48h before expanding.
